concepts.definition: The number that holds which page is shown on the screen; it changes when the time is up or the button is pressed.
concepts.example: sayfa takes the values 0, 1 and 2; sayfaCiz() prepares the two lines to match.
concepts.pitfall: Writing sayfa++ and forgetting to go back to the start; the number goes past the limit and no page is drawn.

concepts.definition: Gives the remainder of a division; it is used to keep a counter going round within a set range.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the % sign means per cent; to write a per cent sign inside text you need %%.

concepts.definition: Adding spaces to the end of short text to cover the old characters on the screen; it flickers less than calling clear().
concepts.example: snprintf(tampon, 17, "%-16s", metin) fills the line to 16 characters.
concepts.pitfall: Not padding; when short text is written over a long one, the old characters stay on the screen.

concepts.definition: snprintf formats text and writes it into a buffer without going past the size; dtostrf turns a decimal number into text.
concepts.example: dtostrf(23.4, 1, 1, t) gives the text "23.4", which is put into the line with %s.
concepts.pitfall: Using %f inside snprintf on the Uno; you get ? instead of the number.

concepts.definition: The page change, the button and the measurement each run with their own millis() timer and without delay.
concepts.example: When simdi - sonSayfa >= 3000, the page is turned; the button turns it straight away in between.
concepts.pitfall: Waiting on the page with delay(3000); the button and the sensor do not work at all during that time.

quiz.prompt:
On a 4-page screen, the page variable is 3 right now. The button was pressed 6 times in a row, and the line below ran on each press. What is the page variable now?

```
sayfa = (sayfa + 1) % 4;
```
quiz.explanation: The order: 3 → 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → 0 → 1. Shortcut: (3 + 6) % 4 = 9 % 4 = 1. Every 4 presses the page returns to its own value, which leaves 2 presses: two steps after 3 is 1.

%d writes the whole number 55, and %% writes a single % sign. The Uno's snprintf cannot write a decimal number with %f and puts ? instead; for a decimal number you first need to turn it into text with dtostrf.

options: Line 2: % 2 should be written instead of % 3
Line 3: sayfaCiz() should not be called
Line 4: delay(3000) stops the program for 3 seconds; the button and the measurement do not work during that time
Line 5: the closing bracket is extra
quiz.explanation: delay(3000) makes the program wait 3 seconds on every round; during that time the button is not read and the sensor is not updated. The fix is to time the page with millis(). The % 3 on line 2 is right for three pages.

quiz.prompt: What is the point of writing each line padded to 16 characters instead of wiping the LCD with lcd.clear() on every update?
options: To stop the screen going blank and flickering, and to let short text cover the old characters
To make the screen look brighter
To speed up the serial port
quiz.explanation: clear() makes the screen blank for a moment and causes flicker. When the line is padded to 16 characters with spaces, the new text completely covers the old one and the screen never goes blank. It has nothing to do with brightness, memory or serial port speed.

quiz.prompt: An OLED screen uses 1 bit of memory for each pixel. How many bytes does the image buffer of a 128x32-pixel screen take up? (1 byte = 8 bits)
quiz.explanation: 128 × 32 = 4096 pixels = 4096 bits; divided by 8 that is 512 bytes. With the same calculation a 128x64 screen holds 1024 bytes, which is half of the Uno's 2048 bytes of memory.
